meaning.zh:
“被解雇” 或 “被炒鱿鱼”。

“Get the sack” 的起源可以追溯到工业革命时期的英国。当一名工人被解雇时，他们会被要求收拾自己的工具和个人物品，通常这些物品会被装进一个麻袋（sack）里带走。久而久之，"get the sack" 就成为了解雇的代名词。
meaning.en: This phrase originates from the period of the Industrial Revolution in Britain. When a worker was dismissed, they were asked to pack up their tools and personal belongings, which would typically be carried away in a sack. Over time, "get the sack" became synonymous with being dismissed from a job.

lines.en: He got the sack after missing several important deadlines.
lines.zh: 他因为错过了几个重要的截止日期而被解雇了。

lines.en: She was worried she'd get the sack if she didn't improve her performance.
lines.zh: 她担心如果不提高表现会被解雇。

lines.en: Getting the sack was a wake-up call for him to take his job seriously.
lines.zh: 被解雇对他来说是一个警钟，提醒他要认真对待工作。
